label: misaligned
reason: LocallyLipschitz uses the ambient MetricSpace distance, which is not required to equal the distance induced by the Riemannian metric g used elsewhere in the definition. On the Euclidean plane, keep g Euclidean and give M the compatible distance rho(a,b)=norm(F(a)-F(b)), where F(x,y)=(x^3,y). The g-distance function f(x,y)=sqrt((x-1)^2+y^2) satisfies the source weak inequality with h=1/f, but near (0,0) its Lipschitz quotient along (epsilon,0) is epsilon/epsilon^3=epsilon^(-2), which is unbounded. Thus the formal predicate rejects a source-admissible distance function, even away from its basepoint.

analysis.first_pass: LocallyLipschitz uses the ambient MetricSpace distance, which is not required to equal the distance induced by the Riemannian metric g used elsewhere in the definition. On the Euclidean plane, keep g Euclidean and give M the compatible distance rho(a,b)=norm(F(a)-F(b)), where F(x,y)=(x^3,y). The g-distance function f(x,y)=sqrt((x-1)^2+y^2) satisfies the source weak inequality with h=1/f, but near (0,0) its Lipschitz quotient along (epsilon,0) is epsilon/epsilon^3=epsilon^(-2), which is unbounded. Thus the formal predicate rejects a source-admissible distance function, even away from its basepoint.
analysis.second_pass: The missing distance link is substantive rather than a consequence of incompatible topology. Pulling back Euclidean distance by the homeomorphism F(x,y)=(x^3,y) produces a genuine metric with exactly the ordinary topology, so the usual smooth atlas, Borel structure, second countability, sigma compactness and Euclidean smooth positive-definite tensor g remain admissible. With p=(1,0), the source distance f=d_g(p,.) is smooth near q=(0,0), yet fails the ambient LocallyLipschitz conjunct at q. The failure therefore persists even if the distance basepoint is removed from the testing domain. In dimension two, h=1/f is locally integrable and Delta_g f=h distributionally, with no atom at p; a direct annular integration-by-parts calculation verifies the source inequality. The formal conjunction is false already at its first clause, independently of any further evaluation of its Laplacian or measure constructors.

counterexample.status: Mathematical separating example checked against the actual input and pinned metric/Lipschitz definitions; not a Lean-kernel-certified construction.
counterexample.manifold: Take a copy M of the ordinary Euclidean plane with its standard topology and smooth atlas, E=H=R^2 with the identity model, and the Euclidean Riemannian tensor g. The copy separates the model-space normed structure from the ambient MetricSpace instance on M.
counterexample.ambient_distance: Set F(x,y)=(x^3,y) and rho(a,b)=||F(a)-F(b)||_2. F is a homeomorphism of the ordinary plane, so rho is a genuine metric inducing the same topology. Its pullback metric can be installed while retaining the existing topology via MetricSpace.induced and Topology.IsEmbedding.comapMetricSpace / MetricSpace.replaceTopology. No change to g or the smooth atlas is required.
counterexample.structural_hypotheses: The ordinary plane is nonempty, Hausdorff, second countable and sigma compact; its model is finite-dimensional of nonzero rank and boundaryless. Compatible-metric replacement preserves the topology and Borel structure. The Euclidean tensor is smooth, symmetric and positive definite. The metric rho is even complete, since F is an onto isometry from (M,rho) to the Euclidean plane, although source completeness is not required by this root.
counterexample.functions: Let p=(1,0), f(x,y)=d_g(p,(x,y))=sqrt((x-1)^2+y^2), and h=1/f away from p with h(p)=0. In dimension n=2 this is exactly the source right-hand side (n-1)/f.
counterexample.source_regularity: The triangle inequality makes f globally 1-Lipschitz for d_g. The Euclidean Ricci tensor is zero. The local integral of h over a disk of radius R centered at p is 2*pi*R, so h is locally integrable. f is bounded on compact sets, and the source test integrals are well-defined.
counterexample.distributional_check: Away from p, Delta_g f=1/f. For a compactly supported smooth test function phi, apply Green's identity outside a disk of radius epsilon centered at p. The inner boundary contribution to integral(f Delta phi - phi Delta f) is the integral over the circle of phi - epsilon*partial_r(phi). Its absolute value is at most 2*pi*epsilon*(sup|phi|+epsilon*sup|grad phi|), tending to zero. Local integrability then gives integral f Delta phi = integral h phi. There is no additional point mass at p, so the source weak inequality holds, in particular for every nonnegative test function.
counterexample.formal_failure: At q=(0,0), for 0<epsilon<1, f(q)=1 and f(epsilon,0)=1-epsilon, while rho(q,(epsilon,0))=epsilon^3. Their Lipschitz quotient is epsilon^(-2). Every rho-neighborhood of q contains (epsilon,0) for all sufficiently small positive epsilon, so no finite local Lipschitz constant exists. LocallyLipschitz f is false, hence WeakLaplacianLE is false already at its first conjunct.
counterexample.robustness: The failure occurs at q, distinct from the distance basepoint p; f and h are smooth near q. It is not an artifact of the singularity of 1/f, disconnectedness, a boundary point, a nonstandard topology, or zero/unnormalized measure. A positive common Haar normalization only scales both source test integrals equally.
counterexample.scope: The example uses the actual metric-distance function specified by the bound source, not an unrelated arbitrary function. It demonstrates a mismatch in the weak-inequality predicate, not a failure of the source Calabi comparison theorem.
